excluded_data: Candidate RV signals in ε Tau (872 d, 16 d, 15 d), 11 Com (434 d, 198 d), 24 Boo (65 d and 149 d) and ω Ser (40.54 d, 1852 d): not confirmed as planets, no Table 3/4 parameters, so no rows.
41 Lyn b and 14 And b are questioned in the text because of BIS correlation, but Table 3 still reports their parameters, so they keep rows.

Long-term RV trends (HD 5608, κ CrB, HD 167042, 18 Del, HD 208897) are not separate companions; only the implied outer-companion mass-separation constraints are given, so no extra rows. Trend terms are columns of Table 3.
HD 14067 b alternative orbit solution from Wang et al. (2014) is discussed but not fitted here as separate parameters.
Table 1 (stellar parameters) and Table 2 (data acquisition) contain host-star properties only, so no planet rows.
Stars not revisited (HD 119445, HD 100655, HD 40956, HD 111591) and the planet-population sample in Section 7 from Exoplanet.eu/NASA archive are not planned.
Single-instrument alternative Keplerian fits for HD 32518 and ω Ser (Fig. 31) are text-only comparisons, not tabulated solutions.
Dynamical-mass constraints for outer companions (Fig. 6) are not tabulated.
notes: One row per planet solution; 32 host systems. Table 3 gives RV-only fits for 37 planets across 32 systems. Table 4 gives joint RV+astrometry fits for HD 5608 B (stellar companion, only solution), and for HD 14067 b, HD 120084 b, HD 175679 b, each also in Table 3, so those three get two bracket-labelled solutions. 75 Cet c is the new planet.
